1.w: And Zophar the Naamathite answered and said:

2.w: “So my anxious thoughts make me answer, because of my urgency within me.

3.w: The rebuke of my shaming I have heard, and a spirit from my understanding answers for me.

4.w: This do you know from long ago, from the placing of man upon the earth,

5.w: that the triumph of the wicked is brief, and the rejoicing of the godless is for a moment?

6.w: Though his loftiness should go up to the heavens, and his head should touch to the clouds,

7.w: like his dung, forever he will perish; those having seen him will say, ‘Where [is] he?’

8.w: Like a dream he will fly away and they will not find him; indeed he will be made to wander like a vision of the night.

9.w: The eye [that] saw him will not continue, and his place will not behold him again.

10.w: His children will recompense the poor, and his hands will return his wealth.

11.w: His bones are full of his vigor, and upon the dust it will lie down with him.

12.w: Though evil is sweet in his mouth, [and] he hides it under his tongue,

13.w: he has pity on it and does not forsake it, and he withholds it in the midst of his palate.

14.w: His food is turned over in his belly, [and] the venom of cobras [is] within him.

15.w: He swallows wealth and vomits it; from his belly God expels it.

16.w: The poison of cobras he will suck, [and] the tongue of a viper will kill him.

17.w: He shall not look on streams, [or] rivers [with] torrents of honey and cream.

18.w: He will return his gain and not consume it; he will not rejoice from the wealth of his exchange.

19.w: For he has crushed [and] forsaken the poor; he has seized a house, and he did not build it.

20.w: For he has not known quiet in his belly, [and] with his desiring he will not deliver himself.

21.w: There is no remnant for him to eat; [and] upon thus his prosperity will not endure.

22.w: In the fullness of his sufficiency there will be distress for him; every hand of toil will come [upon] him.

23.w: It will come to pass at the filling of his belly, that [God] will send forth against him the burning of His anger, and will rain upon him into his bowels.

24.w: He will flee from a weapon of iron; a bow of bronze will pierce him through.

25.w: It is drawn and comes out from [his] back, and the gleaming point from his gall; terrors shall come over him.

26.w: Complete darkness is hidden for his treasuring; a fire [that is] not fanned will consume him, the remnant in his tent will be devoured.

27.w: The heavens will uncover his iniquity, and the earth will rise up against him.

28.w: The flood will roll away his house, flowing away on the day of His anger.

29.w: This [is] the portion of a wicked man from God, and the heritage appointed to him from God.”
